boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments at John Brown University, ranging from reservable library rooms and quiet indoor work areas to tables overlooking campus.

cards.title: Settle In With a Desk and Charger
cards.subtitle: Inside Walker Student Center
cards.notes: Bring your device and choose an individual desk or group table; use the charging station, and keep personal electronics with you.
cards.short_summary: A commuter-focused workspace with desks, group tables, lockers, appliances, and device charging.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU identifies the lounge as a place for commuters to study and lists individual study desks, group tables, lockers, and a charging station among its amenities.
cards.access_notes: Dedicated to commuter students. Lockers are first-come, first-served; JBU does not publish lounge hours on this page.

cards.title: Spread Out Near the Library
cards.subtitle: Tables and couches outside Mark Simmons Library
cards.notes: Use a table for group work or take a couch between classes; the library and Media Lab are immediately nearby when you need support.
cards.short_summary: A quiet lobby suited to homework and group projects, with tables, couches, and nearby academic services.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU describes the LRC Lobby as a quiet place for group projects or homework and documents tables, couches, vending machines, and proximity to the library and Media Lab.
cards.access_notes: Located outside the library. JBU does not state separate lobby access hours on the cited page.

cards.title: Build a Research Base on Either Floor
cards.subtitle: Inside the Mabee Learning Resource Center
cards.notes: Choose a desk or study center, then use library computers or ask a librarian for research help when an assignment needs stronger sources.
cards.short_summary: JBU’s primary library combines individual work areas, research collections, computers, and staff assistance.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU says Mark Simmons Library supports university research needs; its commuter guide documents desks and study centers, while its library sheet confirms computers on both floors.
cards.access_notes: JBU lists regular LRC hours as Monday–Wednesday 7:30 a.m.–2 a.m.; Thursday 7:30 a.m.–midnight; Friday 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m.; Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sunday 2 p.m.–2 a.m.

cards.title: Reserve a Room for Focused Work
cards.subtitle: Individual, group, and presentation-practice rooms
cards.notes: Reserve ahead through EagleNet or at the circulation desk for collaboration or presentation practice; otherwise check for an unused room.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms support solo work, group collaboration, and technology-assisted presentation rehearsal.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU documents library study rooms for individuals or groups, including technology-equipped spaces, with advance reservations through EagleNet or the circulation desk.
cards.access_notes: Reserve at the circulation desk or through EagleNet. Unreserved rooms are available first-come, first-served when not in use.

cards.title: Switch Between Computers and Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Soderquist Business Center
cards.notes: Choose a computer station or table for individual work, then move into a study room when a private or group session makes more sense.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated honors space offering tables, computers, soft seating, and private or group study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU states that the Honors Center has tables and computer stations for studying plus study rooms for private or group sessions.
cards.source_title: The Honors Scholars Program at John Brown University
cards.access_notes: For the honors community. JBU lists hours as 7 a.m.–11 p.m. weekly and 7 a.m.–midnight on weekends.

cards.title: Rehearse the Group Presentation
cards.subtitle: Collaborative room in the College of Business
cards.notes: Bring your project team here to work through shared material or practice a presentation before class; confirm availability inside the building.
cards.short_summary: A business-school meeting room explicitly designated for projects, presentation practice, and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU identifies the Soderquist Business Center meeting room as a space where students can collaborate on group projects, practice presentations, and study.
cards.access_notes: The cited page does not publish hours or a reservation method; verify room availability and class-related access on site.

cards.title: Take the Project Into the Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Study space in the College of Business
cards.notes: Use the room for pre-class review, collaborative project work, or a presentation run-through; check locally before planning a group session.
cards.short_summary: A named reading room documented for studying, project collaboration, and presentation preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU describes the Soderquist Business Center reading room as a place for students to collaborate, practice presentations, and study before or after class.
cards.access_notes: The cited page does not state hours or reservation requirements; building and room availability may follow class schedules.

cards.title: Work Where Engineering Teams Meet
cards.subtitle: Classroom open beyond class times for eligible students
cards.notes: Use the classroom outside scheduled classes for engineering coursework or team projects, and leave promptly if the room is needed for instruction.
cards.short_summary: A technology-center classroom available beyond class periods for coursework, group projects, and study.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU states that the Balzer Technology Center classroom is open beyond class times for engineering and construction management students to work or study.
cards.source_title: Science, Technology, Engineering and Math at John Brown University
cards.access_notes: Limited to engineering and construction management students outside class times; no public hours or reservation procedure is stated.

cards.title: Take Your Notes Out to the Balcony
cards.subtitle: Outdoor tables and chairs overlooking campus
cards.notes: Choose a table in suitable weather for reading or laptop work, and move indoors if wind, rain, or glare makes materials difficult to manage.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor balcony seating provides tables, chairs, and an elevated campus view for fair-weather study.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU recommends the Walker Student Center balconies among its campus study areas and specifically documents tables and chairs there.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor and weather-dependent. The cited page does not state balcony hours; access depends on Walker Student Center availability.

cards.title: Use a Campus Computer for Late Work
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Walker Student Center
cards.notes: Head to the second floor when an assignment requires a campus computer; save work to OneDrive and confirm any software needs before starting.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor student computer lab with published access extending to 2 a.m. on several days.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU’s current commuter resources page places the Computer Lab on Walker Student Center’s second floor and publishes student access hours.
cards.access_notes: JBU lists Sunday 2 p.m.–2 a.m.; Monday–Wednesday 7:30 a.m.–2 a.m.; Thursday 7:30 a.m.–midnight; Friday 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m.; Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.
